content:
Now that PR#1447 (parameterize Dimension over a basis B) has landed, I'd like to finish the other half: the typed unit side is still welded to the default basis. Dimension B is generic and the PR added the magnitude twin UnitScale B (with dimScale proved once via Finset.prod).

However, UnitChoices is a bespoke five-field record fixed to LTMCTDimensionBase, and its dimScale is a hand-rolled copy of that same law. So a typed unit choice over any other basis — e.g. SI's seven ISQ base quantities — is currently inexpressible, even though the dimension side already supports it (ISQDimensionBase, ISQBridge). I filed issue #1480 for this.

The plan is Option D from the PR#1447 review: attach to a basis B a family of typed unit types via a UnitSystem B class, and project that typed layer onto the existing UnitScale B — keeping both basis-genericity and typed-unit safety, with a single source of truth for the scaling law.

I've implemented it on a branch (builds green, all linters pass, axioms classical-only), in three reviewable steps:

  1. Additive core — class UnitSystem B (Unit : B → Type, mag, mag_pos), TypedChoice B := (b : B) → UnitSystem.Unit b, TypedChoice.toScale : TypedChoice B → UnitScale B, the LTMCTDimensionBase instance, and a lemma that the hand-rolled five-factor dimScale equals the generic Finset.prod fold (so no duplicated law). Zero churn to existing call sites.
  2. Rename UnitChoices → LTMCTUnitChoices. It's inherently the unit choice for LTMCTDimensionBase (its fields hardcode the five …Unit types), so the name should mirror the dimension basis. Stays a record — { SI with length := … }, u.length, @[ext] all unchanged.
  3. Second basis — SIUnitChoices := TypedChoice ISQDimensionBase: the typed SI unit choice over the seven ISQ base quantities, from the same machinery. Adds the three ISQ unit types not yet present (CurrentUnit / AmountUnit / LuminousIntensityUnit), a coherent SIUnitChoices.SI (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd), and its dimScale comes for free from UnitScale.dimScale. This is the payoff: ISQDimensionBase ↔ SIUnitChoices sits beside LTMCTDimensionBase ↔ LTMCTUnitChoices, with the existing ltmctToISQ / isqToLTMCT already bridging the bases.

Two things I'd value input on before I open the PR: (a) the naming — LTMCTUnitChoices / SIUnitChoices — and (b) whether to land this as one PR or split it (core / rename / second basis). Happy to adjust.

This all looks good to me. A couple of points:

  1. Do we actually still need LTMCTUnitChoices? Or could we just use TypedChoice LTMCTDimensionBase everywhere (likewise with SIUnitChoices).
  2. Things usually go along easier if split into smaller PRs.

Thanks @Joseph Tooby-Smith — I've answered both of your points directly on the PR, so the discussion stays next to the code instead of split across two places:

https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/pull/1481#issuecomment-5168463080

TL;DR: keep LTMCTUnitChoices / SIUnitChoices as the named instances of the generic TypedChoice engine — equivTypedChoice + dimScale_eq_toScale_dimScale certify they carry the same data and the same law, and the record keeps the { SI with … } ergonomics the WithDim files rely on. The single-definition dimScale collapse (which would invert the module layering) is deferred to a focused follow-up PR, and I'd keep this PR as one unit since the three commits are intermingled. Full reasoning + code snippets are in the PR comment.
Apologies for the delay @Nicolas Rouquette , I will review your PR based on the comments given here
